worse_pages.note: In the first block of the table the halves (D, IↃ, I⊐, QC) are paired with the wrong thousand-signs, one row too high; the rest of the table and the closing sentence match the page.

The scan cuts off the right edge of the text block. The transcription fills in some lost word endings without saying so, and drops others: 'sine' before 'ulla intermissione' and 'fide' after 'nudaque'.

The transcription pane is blank apart from a tool-error note, while the image shows page 37: a printed table of millenary numeral signs (M, CIↃ, ∞, X̄, CCCIↃↃↃ…) with their values 1000–1000000 and half-values 500–500000, followed by two lines of Latin text.

The page clearly shows printed Latin text on how to arrange the numbers in the magic square of Jupiter ('quadratum Iouis', sum 34, total 134), page 85 with a side note, but the candidate has no text at all and falsely calls the page an illegible handwritten manuscript.
This is a complete and accurate transcription of p. 48. The only slips are 'celebrandi' where the page has 'celebranda' and an odd glyph in 'Biblicus'.
The transcription follows the page closely, line by line, including the italic commentary at the top and bottom. The only slip is one obvious typo, 'egressronis' for 'egressionis'.

In the Commentum, about four lines are missing (the Isaiah 64 gloss and the whole Jeremiah 3 passage). The text on either side is joined so that Jerome's words seem to continue straight into 'qui nolunt ad meliora conuerti', which is not what the page says.

The page shows p. 82 of a Latin polemical letter ('Epistola Tertia') arguing about syllogisms and the Austrian baptismal Agenda, but the transcription prints an unrelated De re metallica passage with an invented woodcut.

The text matches the page line for line. The only slips are long-s read as f in 'luminofa' and 'ſuaviffimum', the page's misprint 'experimut' silently corrected, and italics that cover more words than the page does.

The main text matches the page closely, but nine of the ten marginal notes are missing, including the 'Arbor Porphyrij' labels (Substantia, Corpus, Animal, Homo and others), and the initial is wrongly described as a V.
The table pairs most of the half-notes in the first group (1000s) with the wrong whole-number symbols, and it adds two ↀ rows that are not on the page. The rest of the text and numerals are right.
The scan is cropped on the right. The transcription quietly fills in the cut-off words, and it drops the cut-off 'sine' before 'ulla intermissione', which reverses the sense.
The table's numbers are right, but the 500 half-notes are listed one row too high next to the wrong 1000 symbols. One symbol, CXƆ, is printed as CXD, and the stray "tes" fragment is tagged as meta.

The text follows the page in order, but the right edge of the page is cropped, and the candidate silently fills in the missing words. It also loses the word before 'ulla intermissione', which garbles that phrase.
